info.name: Walnut Technologies — Website & Admin API
info.description:
# Walnut Technologies API collection

Every endpoint served by **https://walnut-technologies.vercel.app** — the marketing site, the admin UI and the admin API on one origin.

## Run order

1. Open **collection variables** and set `email` / `password` (your admin login).
2. Set `ingest_key` = the `LEADS_INGEST_KEY` env var (only needed for the leads-ingest request).
3. Run `1 · Authentication → Sign in`. Postman stores the cookies; the rest of the collection works.

## Base URLs

| variable | value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://walnut-technologies.vercel.app` |
| `admin_api` | `{{base_url}}/admin/api` — use this, cookies are scoped to `/admin/api` |
| `site_api` | `{{base_url}}/api` — website-only endpoints (contact form) |

## Three services, one origin

```vercel.json rewrites
/                 → website (static Vite build)
/admin/*          → admin_ui  (React SPA)
/admin/api/*      → admin_api (Express)   ← cookie path matches here
/api/contact      → admin_api (contact handler mounted on Express)
/*                → website
```

## How data is collected

1. **Visitor submits a form** on the website → `POST /api/contact`.
2. The handler validates (CORS allow-list, 5/min rate limit, honeypot, 3 s–1 h timing window, length caps), sanitises, then in parallel:
   - sends an email via **Resend** (reply-to = visitor), and
   - POSTs to `/admin/api/public/leads` with `x-ingest-key` → a **Lead document in MongoDB** (`walnut_admin`).
3. It only reports failure if *both* channels fail, so one outage never loses the enquiry.
4. The **admin Leads inbox** reads those documents (role-scoped), and `GET /leads/export.csv` exports them.

## How content is updated

`PUT /content/:key` saves a draft → `POST /content/publish` promotes every changed section, fires `VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` (a new Vercel build, ~40 s) and records a version. The build runs `scripts/fetch-content.mjs`, which GETs `/admin/api/public/content` and writes `src/data/content.json` before `vite build`.

## Auth, in one paragraph

httpOnly cookies `wa_access` (15 min) and `wa_refresh` (12 h / 30 min idle), scoped to `/admin/api`. Every mutating request also needs `x-requested-with: walnut-admin` — the collection adds it automatically at the root, so inherited auth covers the whole set. Superadmins must enrol MFA. Roles are enforced server-side by `requirePermission()`.

## Rate limits

| endpoint | limit |
|---|---|
| `POST /auth/login`, `/login/mfa`, `/reset`, `/password`, `/accept-invite` | 20 / 15 min |
| `POST /auth/forgot` | 5 / hour |
| `POST /api/contact` | 5 / min per IP |
| `POST /admin/api/public/leads` | 60 / min |

Returned as `Ratelimit` / `RateLimit-Policy` headers (draft-7).

variable.description: Returned by POST /auth/login when MFA is on

item.name: 0 · Start Here
item.description:
Two requests that need **no login** — run them first to confirm the base URL and connectivity.

- `GET /healthz` — liveness probe of the admin API.
- `GET /admin/api/public/content` — the published CMS snapshot. This is the **same endpoint the website build reads** `scripts/fetch-content.mjs` calls it during `npm run build` when `CMS_API_URL` is set.

Next: open **1 · Authentication** and run *Sign in*. Postman stores the `wa_access` / `wa_refresh` cookies automatically, so every other folder just works afterwards.

request.description:
Liveness endpoint mounted in `app.js`. Returns `{"ok":true}` with 200.

No authentication, no cookies, no CSRF header. If this fails, nothing else on the origin will work.

Returns **published** content only — drafts never leave the admin (`publishedSnapshot()`).

Consumers:
1. `scripts/fetch-content.mjs` at build time — writes `src/data/content.json` before every Vercel build.
2. The live website at runtime.

Response: `{ generatedAt, content }` where `content` holds the 13 sections: `brand, about, trustSignals, divisions, products, process, industryFourTechnologies, impactBenefits, expertise, clientSectors, resources, news, chatbot`.

CORS: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is echoed only for origins in `PUBLIC_CORS_ORIGINS`. Cache-Control: `no-store`.

response.name: 200 — snapshot
response.body: {"generatedAt":"2026-10-16T06:55:31.829Z","content":{"brand":{"name":"Walnut Technologies","fullName":"Walnut Technologies Pvt. Ltd.","tagline":"Electronics for the World"},"about":{},"trustSignals":{},"divisions":[],"products":[],"process":[],"industryFourTechnologies":[],"impactBenefits":[],"expertise":[],"clientSectors":[],"resources":[],"news":[],"chatbot":{}}}

item.name: 1 · Authentication (cookie session)
item.description:
**How sign-in works**

1. `POST /auth/login` with `{ email, password }`.
   - No MFA → `200 { user }` and two **httpOnly cookies** are set.
   - MFA on → `200 { mfaRequired: true, challenge }` — pass that challenge to step 2.
2. `POST /auth/login/mfa` with `{ challenge, code }` (or `recoveryCode`) → session.

**Cookies** (`lib/sessions.js`)

| cookie | path | lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| `wa_access` | `/admin/api` | 15 min (JWT, HS256) |
| `wa_refresh` | `/admin/api/auth` | 12 h absolute, 30 min idle |

They are scoped to `/admin/api`, which is why this collection always calls `{{admin_api}}` — call `/api/...` instead and the cookie will not be sent.

**CSRF**: Header `x-requested-with: walnut-admin` is applied automatically from the collection-level auth. Every non-GET under `/admin/api` and `/api` rejects requests without it (403 `CSRF`).

**Mandatory MFA**: a `superadmin` who has not enrolled can only reach the MFA-setup routes; everything else answers `403 MFA_SETUP_REQUIRED`.

Postman: after *Sign in*, run *Get current user* to verify the session.

request.description:
Rate limit: **20 attempts / 15 min** per IP (`Ratelimit` headers are returned).

Body: `email` (lowercased, max 254), `password` (1–200).

Responses:
- `200 { user }` — signed in, cookies set.
- `200 { mfaRequired: true, challenge }` — continue with *Sign in with TOTP*.
- `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS` — wrong password or inactive account (bcrypt always runs, so timing does not leak whether the email exists).
- `401 LOCKED` — 5 failed attempts locks the account for 15 minutes.
- `400 VALIDATION` — missing/invalid fields.

Run this **first**; Postman saves the cookies for every other request.

Use the `challenge` returned by *Sign in* when the account has MFA enabled. The challenge is a short-lived JWT (5 min) bound to that user.

Send either `code` (6-digit TOTP) **or** `recoveryCode` (one-time, consumed on use).

Errors: `401 CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`, `401 INVALID_CODE`, `401 LOCKED`.

Rotates the refresh token: the old `wa_refresh` is invalidated and a new pair of cookies is issued.

If a **already-rotated** refresh token is replayed, the server treats it as theft and revokes the session (`401 SESSION_ENDED`, logged as `refresh-token reuse detected`).

Errors: `401 SESSION_ENDED` when missing/expired/revoked.
Revokes the session referenced by `wa_refresh` and clears both cookies. Always `200 { ok: true }`.

Returns the signed-in profile plus the role’s permission list.

Marked `allowWithoutMfa`, so a superadmin who has not enrolled MFA can still read their own profile.

Run it **before** signing in to see the 401 shape (saved example), and again after *Sign in*.

Rate limit: **5 / hour**.

Always answers `200 { ok, message }` whether or not the account exists, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts. When it does exist a token is stored (hashed) and an email with `{APP_URL}{ADMIN_PATH}/reset-password?token=…` is sent through Resend. Reset link TTL: 30 minutes.

Consumes the one-time token, applies the password policy, clears lockout counters and **revokes every session** of that user.

Errors: `400 TOKEN_INVALID` (unknown/used/expired), `400 WEAK_PASSWORD`.
Read-only check used by the accept-invite screen. Returns `{ name, email }`, or `400 TOKEN_INVALID`.
Sets the password, flips `status: invited → active`, consumes the token and **signs the user in immediately** (cookies returned). Rate limit: 20 / 15 min.

Requires the session cookie. Verifies the current password, enforces the password policy, then revokes **all other sessions** (this one survives).

Errors: `400 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `400 WEAK_PASSWORD`, `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`.
Generates a TOTP secret (stored encrypted) and returns `{ qrDataUrl, secret }`. Nothing is enabled yet — the secret sits in `mfa.pendingSecretEnc` until *enable* succeeds.

Confirms the first TOTP code, promotes the pending secret, generates **10 one-time recovery codes** and returns them (`{ recoveryCodes, user }`). Existing sessions other than this one are revoked.

Errors: `400 INVALID_CODE`, `400 Start the setup again`.
Requires password **and** TOTP. Superadmins cannot disable MFA — they get `403 Two-factor authentication is mandatory for Super Admins`.
Invalidates all previous recovery codes and returns a fresh set of 10.
Active sessions for this user: `{ id, ip, userAgent, createdAt, lastUsedAt, current }`, newest first.
Signs out another device. Returns `{ ok: true }`; the victim’s next request gets `401 SESSION_ENDED`.

item.name: 2 · Contact form (website visitor → email + leads inbox)
item.description:
**How a visitor submission travels**

```
Browser form  →  POST {base_url}/api/contact        (api/contact.js, mounted on the Express app)
                     ├─ guards: CORS origin allow-list · 5 req/min/IP · honeypot ·
                     │          formTime window (3 s – 1 h) · field length caps · sanitising
                     └─ in parallel:
                        ├─ RESEND  → real notification email (reply-to = visitor)
                        └─ POST {CMS_API_URL}/api/public/leads  (header x-ingest-key)
                                    → Lead document in MongoDB  →  admin Leads inbox
```

Both channels run through `Promise.allSettled`: the visitor is only failed if **both** fail, so a Resend outage still stores the lead (and vice-versa).

Only **one** of the two deliveries is enough for `200 { success: true }`.

⚠️ The first request below is a real submission: it sends an actual email and creates a real lead. Use it deliberately.

item.name: ⚠️ Submit a form (sends a real email)

request.description:
⚠️ **Side effects**: sends a real email through Resend *and* creates a lead in the admin inbox.

`type` ∈ `contact | quote | resource | application` (anything else is coerced to `contact`).

Guards, in order:
1. **Origin** — if an `Origin` header is present it must be on the allow-list (`walnut-technologies.vercel.app`, `www.…`, `localhost:3000/3001/5173`). *Postman sends no Origin by default, which is treated as allowed.*
2. `Content-Type` must contain `application/json` → else `415`.
3. Body ≤ 4 MB → else `413`.
4. **Rate limit 5/min per IP** → `429`.
5. **Honeypot** — any truthy `website` field returns `200` but stores nothing (bot trap).
6. **formTime** — browser sends `Date.now()` at page load; server rejects `< 3 s` (too fast to be human) or `> 1 h` (stale). Leave it `""` in testing to skip the check.
7. `name` + `email` required, `message` required (unless `type: application`), email regex, per-field length caps.
8. `resume` — base64, max 3 MB, `type: application` only.

Response: `200 { success: true, message }`. On total failure `503` (not configured) or `500`.

body.raw:
{
  "type": "contact",
  "name": "Postman Test",
  "email": "postman@example.com",
  "phone": "",
  "company": "",
  "subject": "API collection test",
  "message": "Sent from the Postman collection while checking the API.",
  "quantity": "",
  "resourceTitle": "",
  "jobTitle": "",
  "website": "",
  "formTime": "",
  "resume": null
}

response.name: 429 — rate limited
response.body: {"error":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}

request.description:
Negative test: an `Origin` outside `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is answered `403` before anything else runs — no email, no lead.

A *missing* Origin is allowed; only a **known-but-disallowed** origin is refused.
The handler only implements `POST` and `OPTIONS`; anything else returns `405`.

item.name: 3 · Public API (website ↔ server, no session)
item.description:
Endpoints the **website itself** calls. They never use cookies:

- `GET /public/content` — the published CMS snapshot (build + runtime).
- `POST /public/leads` — server-to-server ingest from `/api/contact`, protected by the shared `LEADS_INGEST_KEY` compared with a constant-time `safeEqual`.
- `GET /media/:id/:filename` — public image delivery straight from GridFS, `immutable` cached for 1 year.

Rate limit on lead ingest: **60/min**. Body limit 6 MB (resumes are base64).

request.description: Same request as in *0 · Start Here* — repeated here so this folder reads top-to-bottom. Drafts are never included.

The endpoint `/api/contact` calls internally. Requires header **`x-ingest-key`** matching the `LEADS_INGEST_KEY` env var (Vercel + server must agree).

Validated with Zod: `type` must be one of `contact|quote|resource|application`, `name` ≤ 100, valid `email`, all other fields optional with caps. Optional `resume` = `{ filename, content }` base64 ≤ 4.5 MB → stored in GridFS bucket `resumes`.

Response: `201 { ok: true, id }`.

Set `{{ingest_key}}` in the collection variables before running.

body.raw:
{
  "type": "contact",
  "name": "Postman Test",
  "email": "postman@example.com",
  "phone": "",
  "company": "",
  "subject": "Ingest test",
  "message": "Sent by the Postman collection.",
  "quantity": "",
  "resourceTitle": "",
  "jobTitle": "",
  "ip": "203.0.113.10",
  "resume": null
}

request.description:
Streams the original GridFS object for a media id. Headers: `Content-Type` from the document, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`.

404 when the media document or the GridFS object is gone.

item.name: 4 · Dashboard
item.description:
One aggregate endpoint, shaped by the caller’s role — sections are only included when the role may see them:

- `leads` (needs `leads:read` / `applications:read`): new/week counts, per-type breakdown, 30-day daily series (Asia/Kolkata), 6 most recent.
- `content` (needs `content:read`): keys with unpublished draft changes + last publish (who, when, deploy status).
- `activity` (needs `audit:read`): 8 latest audit entries.

request.description:
Requires a session. Response keys are conditional — a `sales` user gets `leads` only, an `editor` gets `content` only, a superadmin gets everything.

A `viewer` with no leads/content/audit permission receives `{}`.

item.name: 5 · Content / CMS (draft → publish → website rebuild)
item.description:
**The publish pipeline**

```
PUT /content/:key            editor saves a DRAFT (optimistic lock: baseUpdatedAt)
POST /content/publish        publisher flips draft → published for every changed section
        ├─ fires VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL  → new production deployment (~40 s)
        └─ records a ContentVersion (snapshot, changedKeys, note, deploy status)
Build on Vercel:  npm run build → scripts/fetch-content.mjs → GET /admin/api/public/content
        └─ writes src/data/content.json → vite build → site live
```

If `CMS_API_URL` is unset the fetcher skips and the committed `content.json` is shipped. If it is set and the API is unreachable the build **fails on purpose** so stale content is never published as if it were a fresh publish.

Permissions: `content:read` to read, `content:edit` to save/discard, `content:publish` to publish/restore (publisher or superadmin).

**Concurrency**: `PUT /content/:key` is a compare-and-swap — omit `baseUpdatedAt` → `400`; someone else saved meanwhile → `409` with the other editor’s name.

request.description: The Zod-backed definitions for every editable section (key, kind, field rules). The admin UI builds its editors from this.
Every section with its draft, published values and whether they differ — this is how the UI knows what has unpublished changes.
Last 50 versions, newest first, snapshots stripped. Includes `changedKeys`, `note`, `publishedByName` and the `deploy` result.

Returns `{ definition, draft, published, changed, draftUpdatedAt, publishedAt }`.

`draftUpdatedAt` is the value you must echo back as `baseUpdatedAt` when saving.

`body.data` is validated against the section schema → `400 VALIDATION` on a bad shape.

`body.baseUpdatedAt` is **required**: the `draftUpdatedAt` you loaded, or `null` for a section never saved. The update runs as a compare-and-swap on that exact timestamp.

Responses:
- `200 { draft, changed, draftUpdatedAt }`
- `409 CONFLICT` + `meta: { draftUpdatedAt, draftUpdatedBy }` — someone else saved first; reload or overwrite deliberately.
- `400` when `baseUpdatedAt` is missing (deliberate: it is a client bug, not a licence to clobber).

Publishes **every** section whose draft differs from published, then:

1. `triggerDeploy()` POSTs to `VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` → a new production deployment.
2. Creates a `ContentVersion` with the full snapshot, `changedKeys`, your `note` and the deploy result.
3. Writes an audit entry.

Response: `{ version, deploy }`. If `VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` is missing the publish still succeeds but `deploy.status` reports that the website was not rebuilt — that is the “deploy skipped” badge.

Errors: `400 NOTHING_TO_PUBLISH`, `403` without `content:publish`.

Copies that snapshot back into both draft **and** published for every section it contains, triggers a rebuild and records a new version noting where it came from.

Errors: `404 Version not found`.
Resets the section’s draft back to its published value. `200 { draft, changed: false }`. Needs `content:edit`.

item.name: 6 · Leads inbox (where form data lands)
item.description:
**Where every submission ends up.** Rows are created by `POST /admin/api/public/leads` (called from `/api/contact`) with `status: new`.

Role scoping: `sales`/superadmin see `contact | quote | resource`; `hr` sees `application`; `viewer` can read. A type outside your scope answers `403`.

Statuses: `new → contacted → qualified → won | lost`, plus `spam`. `spam` is excluded from listings unless you filter for it explicitly.

Assignments: `sales` (enquiries) and `hr` (applications) are eligible assignees.

request.description:
Paged list. Response: `{ leads, total, page, pages }` where each lead summary is `{ id, type, status, name, email, company, subject, assignedTo, hasResume, createdAt }`.

Ticked-but-disabled parameters are there to discover — enable the ones you need.

query.description: new | contacted | qualified | won | lost | spam

request.description: Active users whose role can own work: `superadmin | sales | hr` → `{ users: [{ id, name, role }] }`.

Same filters as the list, up to 10 000 rows. Returns `text/csv` with a BOM and an attachment filename.

Every cell is quoted and values starting with `= + - @` are prefixed with an apostrophe to block spreadsheet formula injection. Audited as `leads.exported`.
Full lead + `canManage` flag for the caller. Resume is summarised as `{ filename, size }` (the file itself needs the resume endpoint).

`status` must be a valid enum value; `assignedTo` is a user id, `null` to unassign (`400 Unknown user` for an unknown/disabled account).

Needs `leads:manage` (or `applications:manage` for an application lead). Returns `{ ok: true }`.
Text 1–2000 chars, stored with author id/name. `201 { notes }`.
Streams the GridFS `resumes` object as an attachment. `404 No resume attached` when there is none. Audited on every download.
Needs `leads:delete` (superadmin only in practice). Also deletes the stored resume. `404 Lead not found`.

item.name: 7 · Users & roles
item.description:
Whole router is gated by `users:manage` (superadmin).

Roles: `superadmin · publisher · editor · sales · hr · viewer`.

| role | permissions |
|---|---|
| superadmin | `*` (MFA mandatory) |
| publisher | dashboard, content read/edit/publish, media read/manage |
| editor | dashboard, content read/edit, media read/manage |
| sales | dashboard, leads read/manage |
| hr | dashboard, applications read/manage |
| viewer | dashboard, content read, media read, leads read |

Invitations only go to domains in `ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS`. Invite links live 72 h. Active users cannot be deleted — disable them so the audit trail survives.

request.description: All users sorted by status then name. Secrets are stripped (`toSafeJSON`).

Creates a user with `status: invited` and emails an accept link (72 h TTL).

If the email could not be sent (local dev, Resend rejection) the response includes `inviteLink` so you can hand it over manually.

Errors: `400 DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `400 DUPLICATE`.
Rotates the token and re-emails. `400` if the user already accepted.

Guard rails: you cannot change your own role or disable yourself; invited users become active only by accepting; there must always be **one active superadmin**.

Changing a role or disabling a user revokes all of that user’s sessions immediately.
Clears `failedLoginCount` and `lockUntil` after 5 failed logins locked them for 15 minutes.
Turns their TOTP off and revokes every session (they sign in with password only, then re-enrol). Cannot be used on yourself.
Revokes all their sessions except your own if you target yourself. `{ ok: true }`.
Only `status: invited` can be removed. Active users must be disabled instead (`400`), to preserve the audit trail.

item.name: 8 · Media library
item.description:
Uploads are re-encoded with sharp: decoded (anything that is not a real image is rejected), auto-rotated, metadata stripped, capped at 2400 px wide, saved as WebP q82 in GridFS bucket `media`.

Public URL shape: `{APP_URL}/media/{id}/{filename}`.

Permissions: `media:read` to list, `media:manage` to upload/edit/delete. Deleting an image the website still references is refused with `400 IN_USE`.

request.description: Response: `{ media, total, page, pages }`; each item has `id, url, filename, originalName, alt, width, height, size, uploadedByName, createdAt`.

`multipart/form-data` with a single `file` part (15 MB cap) plus optional `alt`.

Response `201 { media }`. Errors: `400 Choose an image to upload`, `400 That file is not a supported image …`.

formdata.description: JPG / PNG / WebP / AVIF / GIF, up to 15 MB

request.description: Only `alt` is editable, max 200 chars.
Removes the GridFS object and the document. Refused with `400 IN_USE` while any draft or published content still points at `/media/{id}/`.

item.name: 9 · Audit log
item.description:
Append-only trail, retained 365 days. Requires `audit:read` (superadmin only, since `sales`/`hr`/`editor` do not hold it).

Actions seen in practice: `auth.login`, `auth.login_failed`, `auth.locked`, `content.saved`, `content.published`, `lead.updated`, `leads.exported`, `media.uploaded`, `user.invited`.

request.description: Response: `{ entries, total, page, pages }`, newest first.

query.description: case-insensitive match on the actor email

item.name: 10 · Error examples (captured from production)
item.description:
Negative tests with **real responses** taken from `https://walnut-technologies.vercel.app`. Useful as regression checks and as a reference for the error contract.

**Uniform error shape** (`lib/http.js`):

```json
{ "error": "human readable message", "code": "MACHINE_CODE" }
```

- `4xx` → the real message.
- `5xx` → always `"Something went wrong. Please try again."` (details only go to the server log).
- `code` present on errors raised through `HttpError`; validation failures use `VALIDATION` and prefix the field (`"email: Required"`).

These requests deliberately disable the collection auth so the header really is missing.

request.description: No cookie → `401`. Cookies are still sent by Postman if you are signed in, so sign out first (or use a fresh workspace) to reproduce.

item.name: 403 when the CSRF header is missing

request.description: Every non-GET under the admin API requires `x-requested-with: walnut-admin`. Removing it (this request has auth disabled) yields `403 CSRF` **before** rate limiting or validation.

item.name: 403 when the ingest key is wrong

request.description: Constant-time comparison against `LEADS_INGEST_KEY`. Rate limit headers show `60/min`.
